title: Introduction to Functions
statement: Determine if a relation, equation, or graph defines a function using the definition as well as the vertical line test.

title: Function Notation
statement: Use and interpret function notation to evaluate a function for a given input value and find a corresponding input value given an output value.

title: Characteristics of a Function's Graph
statement: Use the graph of a function to find the domain and range in interval notation, the x- and y-intercepts, the maxima and minima, and where it is increasing and decreasing using interval notation.

title: Slope and Average Rate of Change
statement: Determine the average rate of change of a given function over a given interval. Find the slope of a line.

title: Equations of Lines
statement: Determine an equation for a line when given two points on the line and when given the slope and one point on the line. Express these equations in slope-intercept or point-slope form and determine the slope and y-intercept of a line given an equation.

title: Graphs of Linear Equations
statement: Graph a line given its equation or some combination of characteristics, such as points on the graph, a table of values, the slope, or the intercepts.

title: Linear Models and Meanings
statement: Build linear models from verbal descriptions, and use the models to establish conclusions, including by contextualizing the meaning of slope and intercept parameters.

title: Graphing Quadratic Functions
statement: Graph quadratic functions and identify their axis of symmetry, and maximum or minimum point.

title: Quadratic Models and Meanings
statement: Use quadratic models to solve an application problem and establish conclusions.

title: Combining and Composing Functions
statement: Find the sum, difference, product, quotient, and composition of two or more functions and evaluate them.

title: Finding the Inverse Function
statement: Find the inverse of a one-to-one function.

title: Transformation of Functions
statement: Apply transformations including horizontal and vertical shifts, stretches, and reflections to a function. Express the result of these transformations graphically and algebraically.

title: Degree and Radian Measure
statement: Convert between degrees and radians. Draw angles in standard position.

title: Angle Position and Arc Length
statement: Identify and find coterminal angles. Find the length of a circular arc.

title: The Unit Circle
statement: Use reference angles, signs, and definitions to determine exact values of trigonometric functions.

title: Properties of Sine and Cosine Graphs
statement: Determine the basic properties of the graphs of sine and cosine, including amplitude, period, and phase shift.

title: Introduction to Exponentials
statement: Determine if a given function is exponential. Find an equation of an exponential function. Evaluate exponential functions (including base

title: Graphs of Exponential Functions
statement: Graph exponential functions and determine the domain, range, and asymptotes.

title: Introduction to Logarithms
statement: Convert between exponential and logarithmic form. Evaluate a logarithmic function, including common and natural logarithms.

title: Graphs of Logarithmic Functions
statement: Graph logarithmic functions and determine the domain, range, and asymptotes.

title: Properties of Logarithms
statement: Use properties of logarithms to condense or expand logarithmic expressions.

title: Solving Exponential and Logarithmic Equations
statement: Solve exponential and logarithmic equations.

title: Applications of Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
statement: Solve application problems using exponential and logarithmic equations.

title: Additional Trigonometric Functions
statement: Graph trigonometric functions including tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant functions and transformations of these functions, and determine the domain and range.

title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
statement: Determine the inverse sine, cosine, and tangent values; graph inverse trig functions and determine the limitations on the domain and range.

title: Solving Right Triangles
statement: Use trigonometric functions and the Pythagorean Theorem to solve right triangles.

title: Trigonometric Laws
statement: Use the law of sines and/or the law of cosines to solve non-right triangles.

title: Applications of Trigonometry
statement: Solve applications that require the use of trigonometry to find a side or angle.

title: Trigonometric Identities
statement: Use the sum and difference, the double-angle, and power-reducing formulas for cosine, sine, and tangent and the Pythagorean identities.

title: Verifying Identities
statement: Symbolically verify identities by using various trig identities.

title: Trigonometric Equations
statement: Find all solutions to a trigonometric equation.

title: Graphs of Polynomial Functions
statement: Determine the zeros and their multiplicities of a polynomial in factored form. Describe and graph the behavior of a polynomial function at the intercepts and the ends.

title: Polynomial Long Division
statement: Rewrite a rational function as a polynomial plus a proper rational function.

title: Zeros of Polynomial Functions
statement: Determine the zeros of a polynomial function with real coefficients.

title: Rational Equations
statement: Solve a rational equation.

title: Graphs of Rational Functions
statement: Find the domain and range, vertical and horizontal asymptotes, and intercepts of a rational function and use this information to sketch the graph.

title: Quadratic Inequalities
statement: Solve quadratic inequalities and express the solution graphically and with interval notation.

title: Quadratic and Rational Inequalities
statement: Solve rational inequalities and express the solution graphically and using interval notation.

title: Linear Equations and Inequalities
statement: Solve a linear equation in one variable. Solve a linear inequality in one variable and express the solution graphically and using interval notation.

title: Applications of Linear Equations
statement: Solve application problems involving linear equations.

title: Distance and Midpoint
statement: Given two points, determine the distance between them and the midpoint of the line segment connecting them.

title: Absolute Value Equations and Inequalities
statement: Solve a linear equation involving an absolute value. Solve a linear inequality involving absolute values and express the answers graphically and using interval notation.

title: Quadratic Equations
statement: Solve quadratic equations using factoring, the square root property, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and express these answers in exact form.

title: Systems of Linear Equations
statement: Solve a system of two linear equations in two variables.

title: Trigonometric Ratios
statement: Use a right triangle to evaluate trigonometric functions.

title: Special Right Triangles
statement: Find exact values of trigonometric functions of special angles (30, 45, and 60).

title: Similar Triangles
statement: Use proportional sides of similar triangles to find unknown lengths.

title: Exponents
statement: Simplify expressions using the laws of exponents, including negative and rational exponents.

title: Algebraic Fractions
statement: Simplify algebraic fractions, solve equations with fractions, and simplify complex fractions.

title: Algebra for Advanced Math
statement: Rationalize, factor, and simplify expressions with fractional exponents, the algebra calculus uses most.
